name: Dipole Antenna
description: A charge driven back and forth along x swings in place, 2.4 units either side of the center, at up to 0.25 c (c = 1, Minkowski metric), and radiates. The arrows show its Liénard–Wiechert field on a resting test charge (retarded: read on the light cone): close by, the Coulomb field of where the charge was; farther out, the 1/r radiation term, proportional to its acceleration, travelling out at c in bands that reverse every half wavelength and repeat every wavelength (c·T = 60). At this speed it is a Hertz dipole: averaged over a period the radiation goes as sin²θ from the axis of motion, strongest across it and nothing along it, which is why a radio mast stands upright. The drive F0·cos(2πt/T) repeats every T = 60 (120 steps); the charge starts at the left end of its swing with u = −F0·dt/2, which cancels the half-step lead of the Euler kicks, so it never drifts. The drive comes from the fixed source far below the view (n = 1) and acts only on the charge with q2 = 1. Beyond c·(K − 1)·dt the charge's motion would be extrapolated uniformly from its oldest stored step; the view stays inside.

forces.name: Drive
forces.expression: n_j * q2_i * vec(F0 * cos(2 * pi * time / T), 0, 0)
